reply.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper

observed.facings.png: A labelled 'south' preview of the whole 4x4 linked atlas on a checkerboard. It shows a thin copper tube with teal verdigris mottling, cut into elbows, tees, crosses, straights and end caps. Round bolted grey-steel plates with a copper dome sit at the junctions, there is one free-standing boss tile, and grey clamp-collar dome caps close the dead ends.
observed.south.png: The same atlas at full 1408 px resolution on transparent alpha. The tube width is uniform, a dark rim line runs on both edges, and the axial highlight runs down the middle, so the tube is symmetric across its axis. Elbows are smooth quarter-circles centred on the pipe axis. Every 3- and 4-way junction and the lone cell carries a bolted ring plate with about eight rivets, a hammered copper dome and a small bent tab. End caps are steel hose-clamp bands with a riveted dome closing the tube. The detail is crisp, with no blur. No backdrop or shadow.
observed.single.png: Identical to south.png: the full atlas at high resolution, sharp, with clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: An offline render at 96 px/cell on a vanilla floor checker, with a vanilla pawn on the right for scale. A 14-cell network of thin copper pipe (about 1/8 of a cell wide) with two tees carrying dome bosses, two rounded corners, three clamp-collar end caps and a lone boss cell. A few straight cells carry a small grey band (clamp or wire) or a patch plate at irregular spacing. Next to the pawn the pipe reads as low floor clutter.
observed.siblings.png: Reference: the industrial sibling (grey steel pipe) in the same network layout at 96 px. Same thinness and the same layout conventions: thin line, small junction nubs, small end stubs.
observed.variants_1.png: The straight-cell variants, horizontal and vertical. Two plain stretches with different mottling, one with a black wire wrap held by a steel worm-drive clamp, and one with a riveted grey steel patch plate showing a round and a square bolt head. All ends match the plain straight in width and shading, so they join seamlessly.
observed.assembled_1.png: The same network as scale.png at 96 px/cell without the pawn. Runs join without visible seams. Hardware (a wire wrap on the up-branch, a clamp right of the second tee, a wrap on the down-branch, a patch plate on the right descender) falls on about 4 of the roughly 12 straight cells at irregular spacing. Bosses are centred on the tee cells, caps sit at cell centres, and the elbows turn on the cell centres.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same network at 48 px/cell. The pipe reads as a thin orange-brown line with a darker rim. Bosses read as small round knobs, and the caps and bands as small grey ticks. Still legible as a pipe network.
observed.assembled_3.png: A zoomed crop at 150 px/cell: a tee going up, a corner, and a tee going down. The copper grain, verdigris, rivets, the clamp's worm-screw and the wire turns are all sharp, with no upscale softness. The pipe stays centred on the cell axes through the elbow and the tees. The end cap is a steel clamp band with a riveted dome. The two reddish rivets on the dome faintly suggest a little helmet.

CAMERA.seen: The card names flat top-down linked pipe as an engine limit. The tube is drawn as flat ground art, and the junction domes and end caps are lit consistently from above.

BORE.seen: No open bore shows anywhere: every dead end is closed by a clamp-collar dome cap, and the junctions are covered by bosses.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1/3 every straight, elbow and tee meets its neighbour at the cell edge on the same axis and at the same width, with no seam, offset or width jump. The variants end exactly like the plain straight.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Each atlas tile's pipe ends exit at the centre of the cell edge for each neighbour in its mask. No stray connector stubs appear on any side without a neighbour.

LAYERS.seen: Bosses, clamps and patch plates draw over the tube. The network is a single flat layer with no misordered parts.

ROTATIONS.seen: One atlas. The tube width, palette, boss design and cap design are identical across every tile and orientation (caps facing N, S, E and W all match).

SIGNATURE.seen: Reads as a joined floor water pipe: straights, elbows, tees and a cross join automatically. Scrap character comes from the bolted scrap-plate bosses, the hose-clamp caps, the wire wrap and the patch plate.

MATERIAL.seen: Oxidised copper with a specular axial highlight, fine grain and teal verdigris blotches. The bosses and clamps read as worn steel. It reads as metal, not paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The tube is about 36/264 of a cell wide and centred on the cell axis. Bosses stay well within the cell, nothing overflows, and it matches the sibling's thinness.

ALPHA.seen: south/single show real transparency around every part, with no ground patch, halo or drop shadow. The measured real alpha is True.

OURS.seen: Bespoke copper strip and salvage fittings, not vanilla or donor art (the vanilla pipe is a different design; the sibling is the mod's own grey industrial pipe).

OWNER_NOTES.seen: 'Blurry when zoomed': assembled_3 at 150 px/cell is crisp. 'Same spot repeats every cell': hardware appears on about 1 straight cell in 3–4 at irregular positions, and the plain stretches differ in mottling. 'Bad art alignment': the tube is uniform, symmetric, and centred through the elbows and tees.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 48 px/cell (assembled_2) the network reads clearly as a line with knob junctions. At 32 px the tube would be about 4–5 px wide, the same thinness as the kept industrial sibling, and should still read as a pipe line (extrapolated: no 32 px panel was given).

reply.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper
reply.image_seen: 1 shows the copper pipe atlas; 2–3 show enlarged elbows, junction bosses and capped ends; 4 shows an assembled run beside a pawn; 5 shows the industrial sibling; 6 shows plain, wire-wrapped and plated variants; 7–8 show connected runs at two scales. The supplied assemblies are explicitly offline renders; the required in-game capture is missing.

concerns.evidence: In south.png and variants_1.png, the copper has mottled green oxidation, dark pitting and uneven worn highlights. Junctions carry weathered bolted plates, while the straight variants add wire binding, a clamp and a rectangular repair plate. These visible details support the specified salvage construction, including its intentionally plain stretches and occasional hardware.

The enlarged end caps in south.png show ribbed clamp collars, projecting fasteners and closed metal domes attached directly to the tube. The upward-facing cap has two reddish bolt heads, but their mechanical setting and the same fittings rotated at other ends make them read as hardware. At assembled scale they read as capped pipe ends.

request.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper

edits.change: No previous prompt or findings exist, so the prompt is written from the description. It states the wanted state for each owner complaint: sharp detail at full zoom, one uniform tube width, symmetric across the axis, elbows bent on the pipe axis, a centred boss on junctions, a bolted clamp-collar cap on dead ends, and plain tube cells with no repeated hardware.

invariants: One oxidised copper tube with fine verdigris grain
Tube is thin and low: about 36 px of a 264 px cell, drawn flat as ground clutter
Tube is symmetric across its axis and the same width in every cell
Every tile meets its cell edge at the same centred position, width and colour, so neighbouring tiles join seamlessly
Elbows are bent on the pipe axis
A bolted scrap-plate boss sits centred on every 3-way and 4-way junction and on the lone cell
A dead end closes with a bolted clamp-collar cap
Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, clean dark outline
request.prompt:
A 4x4 atlas of top-down floor pipe tiles for RimWorld, Scrapper (salvage, junk-built) look, 1408 x 1408 px, 16 cells of 264 x 264 px, transparent background. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, crisp and sharp detail that holds up at full zoom. The pipe is ground clutter, drawn flat, low and thin: the tube is about 36 px wide in a 264 px cell, centred in the cell, and lies under pawns.

Material: one oxidised copper tube with fine verdigris grain, warm copper brown with muted blue-green patina in the crevices. The tube is symmetric across its own axis, with matching highlight and shadow on both sides, and keeps exactly the same width, colour and surface texture in every cell. Plain tube surface only: no repeated blemish, patch or hardware along a straight run. Tube ends meet each cell edge at the exact centre with identical width and colour, so neighbouring cells join without a seam.

The 16 cells follow the RimWorld linked-graphic order, one tile per combination of neighbouring pipes (north, east, south, west):
- lone cell with no neighbours: a short stub of tube with a bolted scrap-plate boss centred on it
- four dead-end cells (one open side each): the tube runs from the open cell edge to the centre and closes with a bolted clamp-collar cap, a riveted steel band around the tube end
- two straight cells: vertical and horizontal, tube running edge to edge through the centre
- four elbow cells: a smooth bend on the pipe axis, the tube curving from one cell edge to the adjacent cell edge through the centre
- four tee cells (three open sides): a bolted scrap-plate boss centred on the junction, with three tube arms leaving it
- one cross cell (four open sides): a bolted scrap-plate boss centred on the junction, with four tube arms leaving it

The scrap-plate boss is a small square of dark riveted steel plate with four bolt heads, centred in the cell and slightly wider than the tube. All hardware is small, flat and low. Overall look: weathered salvage plumbing, believable and tidy, readable at 96 px and 48 px per cell. Transparent background around the tube, no ground, no shadow plate, no text.
